verified_by: 3-state differential (Maven, JDK 11) on the real production XStreamConfig; found end-to-end by bbc_e2e.py
note: First NATIVE-Maven external production case verified (TVRenamer, the other verified case, is Gradle wrapped in a Maven harness). Also the first to show a FRAMEWORK-integrated (Axon) adaptation can be verified, because the adaptation is a plain callable method.
discovery_method: bbc_e2e.py run xstream-... -> mine-commits q='xstream ForbiddenClassException' -> classify (native Maven, production). One of 12 *-ranked candidates.

in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: transitive via an Axon bump (no direct xstream bump)
in_repo_version_transition.bump_commit: axon-spring-boot-starter 4.5(.0) -> 4.5.14 (starter first added at 6375e6a, 2021-05-17; 4.5.14 by the fix b76d747f, 2022-07)
in_repo_version_transition.evidence: The repo never bumped xstream directly, but it bumped axon-spring-boot-starter from 4.5.0 (May 2021) to 4.5.14. Axon 4.5.0 predates xstream 1.4.18 (released 2021-08) and pulled xstream 1.4.17; Axon 4.5.14 declares xstream.version 1.4.19. So the transitive xstream crossed the 1.4.18 boundary WITHIN the repo's own history -> counts as an adaptation-to-a-change (via a transitive dependency).

bump_provenance.summary: There is NO commit that bumps xstream across the 1.4.18 boundary in this repo. At the adaptation commit the boundary-crossing xstream version was never chosen or upgraded by the developer — it arrived transitively through the Axon starter. A later commit made the dependency explicit but pinned it to the SAME version it already had transitively (not a bump).
bump_provenance.how_introduced_transitively: At the fix/adaptation commit b76d747f, no pom declares com.thoughtworks.xstream:xstream at all. The app depends on org.axonframework:axon-spring-boot-starter 4.5.14, and Axon uses XStream as its default event/command serializer, so the starter pulls xstream in transitively. Maven resolves it to xstream 1.4.19 (already past the 1.4.18 default-deny boundary). So the app ran on a post-1.4.18 xstream with no explicit version written anywhere.
evidence: `git show b76d747f:core/pom.xml` and `git show b76d747f:pom.xml` — at the adaptation commit NEITHER declares xstream; the dependency is purely transitive via Axon 4.5.14.

The verification harness had to ADD an explicit depth-1 xstream dep to core/pom.xml precisely because a property/-D override does not otherwise change the transitively-pinned version (see verification.harness_notes).
axon-spring-boot-starter.version (4.5.14) drives the resolved xstream 1.4.19; there is no separate xstream-version bump.
bump_provenance.later_explicit_declaration_note: A LATER commit ad900c2 ('34.5 Minimize Core module dependencies') — which is NOT an ancestor of the adaptation commit b76d747f — adds a direct xstream dependency and a <xstream.version>1.4.19</xstream.version> property. This pins xstream to the SAME 1.4.19 already resolved transitively; it is a dependency-management cleanup done AFTER the break was already adapted, not a version bump and not what triggered the ForbiddenClassException.
bump_provenance.why_it_still_breaks: Because the resolved xstream (1.4.19) is already on the default-deny side of the 1.4.18 boundary, the break is present at runtime the moment the app serializes its own domain type through Axon's XStream — no upgrade event is needed to trigger it. The developer discovered it as a runtime ForbiddenClassException and responded with the adaptation commit b76d747f (which CREATED XStreamConfig).
bump_provenance.consequence_for_the_dataset: The 'library version transition' is implicit in the dependency tree rather than materialized as a diff. The 3-state differential recreates the transition synthetically (pinning xstream 1.4.17 -> 1.4.19 via the harness dep) to isolate the version + the adaptation as the only variables.
bump_provenance.distinct_from_bump_source: This is separate from `bump_source` above: bump_source records where the BEHAVIOURAL BREAK was independently confirmed in the BUMP dataset (apache/logging-chainsaw). It is not a version-bump commit in THIS adaptation repo.

behavioral_break.mechanism: xstream 1.4.18+ default-deny: fromXML on a non-allowlisted class throws com.thoughtworks.xstream.security.ForbiddenClassException. Axon uses XStream as its default event/command serializer, so a plain XStream (no allowlist) rejects the app's own domain types under >=1.4.18.

adaptation.repo_note: A Kirill Kargopolov Axon/CQRS-SAGA course project (Spring Boot + Axon Framework). Multi-module Maven; the shared 'core' module holds the domain types and the XStream config.
adaptation.commit_message: 32.6 Fixing com.thoughtworks.xstream.security.ForbiddenClassException by providing custom XStream bean (#32)
adaptation.xstreamconfig_was_new: XStreamConfig did not exist at the parent commit — it was CREATED in the fix (a Spring @Configuration @Bean producing an allowlisted XStream). At the parent the app relied on Axon's default plain XStream (no allowlist).
adaptation.in_repo_causal_evidence: Commit message names the exact exception and the fix ('providing custom XStream bean').
adaptation.summary: Added a production XStreamConfig @Bean that allowlists the app's domain package on the XStream Axon uses, satisfying xstream 1.4.18 default-deny.

verification.method: 3-state differential at the adapted commit (Maven, JDK 11). Because XStreamConfig is a pure method and did not exist at the parent, the differential contrasts a plain `new XStream()` (a faithful stand-in for Axon's pre-adaptation default) against the production `new XStreamConfig().xStream()`, swapping only the xstream version. This keeps 'only the library version / the adaptation' as the variables, exactly as the 3-state model requires.
verification.test: bbc.XstreamBbcTest (authored; derived from the BUMP failing test's shape — mutate a domain object, round-trip through XStream, assert the field survives).
verification.harness_notes: core/pom.xml edited to: (1) add an EXPLICIT xstream dependency version=${bbc.xstream.version} (a direct depth-1 dep, so the baseline override actually applies — otherwise xstream is pinned to 1.4.19 transitively by Axon); (2) add junit-vintage-engine so a JUnit4 test runs under the project's JUnit5 platform. Preserved in scratchpad/xstream-axon-artshishkin-harness/.
verification.conclusion: Confirmed BBC with a real EXTERNAL native-Maven PRODUCTION adaptation: baseline passes, the same (plain-XStream) code breaks only under xstream >=1.4.18 with a ForbiddenClassException on the app's own domain type, and the production XStreamConfig allowlist resolves it.
